papers.what_it_is: A theory paper on quantum query complexity of simplex finding in hypergraphs: a rank-reduction reduction from triangle finding, a conversion of nested Johnson-graph quantum walks into adaptive learning graphs, and an O(n^2.455) quantum query algorithm for 4-simplex finding.

papers.what_it_is: A theory paper that proves upper and lower bounds on the depth and size of circuits for general unitary synthesis, quantum state preparation and diagonal unitaries under qubit-connectivity constraint graphs (path, grids, trees, expanders, arbitrary connected graphs), with and without ancilla; it has no numerical experiments.

quotes: Theorem 1. Any n-qubit unitary can be implemented by a quantum circuit of depth O(4n/n) and size O(4n) under path constraint.
existing.certainty_reason: Theorem 1 is stated in Section 1; the proof is the path-constraint construction of Appendix B and Theorem 13 (Section 5.2) with Theorem 2.

existing.note: The abstract does say depth can be made polynomial with ancilla, but the body does not prove that for the constraint graphs it studies. Section 1 gives for the path with m ancilla greater than order 2 to the n over 2 only a depth lower bound that is exponential, and the Section 1 discussion of QSP states that grid and tree constraints keep the depth exponential in n regardless of the number of ancilla. The trade-off part (not impaired unless exponentially many ancilla) is supported only for m up to order 2 to the n over 2 (Theorem 2) and, for grids, up to the range in Theorem 3.
existing.value: The authors state in the abstract that with ancilla the circuit depth can be made polynomial and that the space-depth trade-off is not impaired by connectivity constraints unless exponentially many ancillary qubits are available. In the body, Theorem 2 gives depth of order 4 to the n over (n + m) for m up to order 2 to the n over 2 under the path constraint, and the authors state that for quantum state preparation grid and tree constraints make the required depth exponential in n regardless of the number of ancillary qubits.

However, both constantdimensional grid and d-ary tree constraints cause the required circuit depth to become exponential in n, regardless of the number of ancillary qubits.
